final_answer:
PRIVILEGED AND CONFIDENTIAL - ATTORNEY WORK PRODUCT
TO: Margaret Chen. FROM: Associate. RE: Cascade - Review of Saxonbrook (Blackmere "Vanguard") redline of Aug. 12, 2024 Consent Decree, Case 3:23-cv-01847-MO. Redline/email dated Sept. 27, 2024.

1. BOTTOM LINE
(a) The redline is not a reliable redline. Its structure, numbering and "rejected" baseline differ from our Aug. 12 draft, and the email describes ~85 edits (65 "conforming," ~20 substantive). I count 30+ substantive changes, many labeled "conforming," plus untracked deletions. Demand a machine comparison and reserve rights on unflagged changes.
(b) Four of Saxonbrook's changes breach our written walk-away triggers or must-haves: 70/30 allocation (trigger is >67%), several-only liability, deletion of the Ridgecrest guarantee combined with four-installment payment, and early termination (pay-and-walk). Insurance clause 14.2 and confidentiality Art. XVIII independently threaten the Granite Bluff policy (Policy EIL-2019-08834).
(c) Quantified: at 70/30 with the redline's other terms, Cascade's exposure is about $39.14M (remediation $33.25M + net past costs $3.355M + past oversight $0.574M + NRD $1.96M), versus the $32M Board ceiling. Correction to our March 28 memo: its $32.97M "net" baseline subtracts the $1.634M reimbursement twice (the $2.666M past-cost line is already net). True 62/38 baseline is $34.608M, already about $2.6M over authority; Board re-authorization or a revised plan is needed regardless.
(d) Recommendation: reject Tier 1; counter Tier 2; accept ~10 genuine conforming edits.

2. REDLINE INTEGRITY (red flags)
- Party misnamed "Vanguard" in header, caption, signature block and comments; our Aug. 12 signature block does too. Fix.
- Untracked changes vs our draft (confirm by machine compare): dropped our recitals on "chlorinated solvent waste streams" (orig. para. 8) and Ridgecrest "operational oversight" (para. 9); paras. 3, 28, 51, 57, 107, 115-117, 125-128 and 135 (jurisdiction, EPA/DOJ transfer approval, no oversight cap, no NRD credits, payments never excused by force majeure, indemnity of US/State, access/records, covenant by settlors, joint termination); and reworded the reopener (orig. 73(a)-(b)). Site distance and plume direction also differ across original, redline and ROD. Redline baselines also misstate force majeure notice (14 days; ours 7) and reporting (monthly; ours quarterly).
- Comment numbering is non-sequential, and "conforming" labels hide substance: 1.8, 1.12, 3.1, 10.1.1, 10.2.4-10.2.5, 10.4.1, 15.2-15.3, 22.3, 23.1, 23.7, signature title.
- Email-vs-redline mismatches: section numbers cited in email (IV.A, VII.A, XIII.F, etc.) do not match the document (Arts. V-XXI); first installment due 30 days (email) vs 60 days (6.1(b)); cure period 30 days (email) vs 15 days (11.2(a)); NRD project "1,200 ft buffer, 4.3 acres wetland" (email) vs "3.5 acres riparian, tributary" (6.5.2); email says cap on "Vanguard's" indemnity but 13.1 makes Cascade's uncapped and covers Affiliates; email omits 7.2.2, 5.1.3/5.2.2, 6.2, 11.3.2, 14.2's document-sharing, the force majeure financial-inability deletion and 23.7. Email says past-cost papers came "in discovery"; redline says our July 12, 2024 letter, yet our cost file runs through Aug. 2024.
- Assignment appears twice (3.2, Art. XX). Hale says nothing has gone to EPA/DOJ.

3. ISSUE-BY-ISSUE (priority; recommendation)
TIER 1 - REJECT
A. Allocation 70/30 (2.3, 2.27, 5.1, 1.14-1.15, 6.3-6.5; email 1). Walk-away: >67% (62% = $29.45M; 70% = +$3.8M). Factual premises are wrong on the record: ROD Sec. 6.2 expressly did not use duration, and attributes 38% of TCE/PCE mass to Saxonbrook because its wastes were concentrated TCE/PCE (ROD 2.1, 6.1, 6.3), it disposed alone 2014-2017, and pre-2003 contribution was already assigned to Cascade. Email's "lower toxicity" claim contradicts ROD. Caveats: the ROD's 62/38 is EPA's mass apportionment, not binding inter-party allocation; CERCLA 113(f)(1) lets a court use "such equitable factors as the court determines appropriate" (not verified this run; retrieval blocked), and Cascade is owner/operator through 2014 and retained ownership (orig. para. 7). Also Granite Bluff reserves on any allocation beyond the EPA record (ROR 4.4, 5.3): 70% risks coverage. Reject; invite the technical dialogue Hale offered, with Appendix E.
B. Several-only liability (7.1, 7.2.2; email 6; "non-negotiable"). Delete. Our March memo overstates: CERCLA joint and several liability is judge-made, not statutory (Burlington Northern v. United States, 556 U.S. 599 (2009), allows apportionment on a reasonable basis), so cite DOJ practice and ROD 6.1, not a "statutory requirement." Practically, EPA will want each settlor liable for the work and Cascade bears Saxonbrook's default risk. 7.2.2 (no contribution claim against a party that "fully paid its share") would strip Cascade's contribution rights against Saxonbrook/affiliates and breaches Granite Bluff para. 5.3; reject. Fallback: joint and several to the government; inter se contribution by allocation.
C. Installments + deletion of Ridgecrest guarantee (6.1(b)-(c), 17.1-17.2, Ex. C-D; email 2-3; "non-negotiable"). Our limits: <=18 months, <=3 installments, 100% LOC from an A- (S&P) bank, guarantee kept, interest at AFR+200bp. Redline: four installments over 3 years from day 60; no interest; unrated regional bank; no guarantee; first installment ($3.5625M) unsecured; LOC covers only installments 2-4 ($10,687,500), with a 30-day post-default draw lag, no evergreen/non-renewal draw, beneficiary EPA/Trust (not Cascade); 17.1's notice triggers arrive only after value extraction. This is the compounding risk our memo warns of. Reject. Counter only: up to 3 installments in 18 months, 100% LOC (A- bank, evergreen, draw on non-renewal 30 days before expiry, interest), Ridgecrest guarantee retained (negotiate cap upward from $5M toward full deferred amount), plus financial covenants and dividend/recap restrictions. Ridgecrest's reported "operational oversight" supports preserving claims.
D. Early termination (19.1). Reject (trigger no. 5): leaves Cascade "solely responsible," including five-year reviews (ROD Sec. 8) and overruns; our para. 135 required joint termination. Counter: release only on EPA certification plus a premium-based cost-overrun buyout, not pay-and-walk.
E. Insurance 14.2 + related (13, 9.1, 7.2.2, 18). 14.2 bars Cascade from any claim that "could" trigger subrogation against Saxonbrook, affiliates or Ridgecrest and requires releasing subrogation and sharing all insurer correspondence. Granite Bluff states such terms are a potential material breach and grounds for denial (ROR 5.1-5.3), requires its prior written consent to any settlement, and requires disclosure of settlement terms to it. Reject (trigger 4); restore paras. 110-114. Confidentiality (Art. XVIII, $250,000 per breach) conflicts with the ROR (no confidentiality barring disclosure to insurer) and with lodging/public comment under CERCLA 122(d)(2) and 28 C.F.R. 50.7 (30 days); reject, or limit to negotiation communications with express insurer/government carve-outs and no liquidated damages. Action: send Granite Bluff the draft and redline now; confirm renewal of the claims-made policy (period ends Oct. 1, 2024) and obtain consent.
F. Contribution protection scope (9.1; 2.1; 23.7; email 7). Reject. 113(f)(2) protects a person who has resolved liability in a judicially approved settlement as to "matters addressed"; parties cannot confer it on non-settling affiliates, parent entities or portfolio companies, and 9.1 also deletes "matters addressed" and bars claims on all Facility matters. It would bar Cascade/Granite Bluff claims against Ridgecrest (ROR 5.2). Restore orig. paras. 76-80. Strike Affiliate benefits in 13.1, 20.2, 23.7.
G. Covenant not to sue and reopeners (8.1-8.2; email 8). Deleting the unknown-conditions and new-information reopeners and extending to RCRA/CWA/state law and "known or unknown" claims is, I believe, contrary to 122(f)(6) and DOJ practice (verification of statutory text and DOJ model not completed this run); DOJ will refuse to lodge. Reject; restore orig. 73-75. Do not tell Hale "the government says" unless EPA/DOJ actually has said so (see Sec. 5).

TIER 2 - COUNTER
H. Past response costs (6.3, 2.19, Ex. E; email 4). Redline: 30% x $3.15M = $945,000 vs $1,634,000 (-$689,000). $680,000 insurance-coverage fees: concede; Exhibit D of our draft expressly listed coverage litigation fees, which was a drafting error; Key Tronic v. United States, 511 U.S. 809 (1994) denies PRP litigation-type fees (recalled; not verified this run). $470,000 security: defend; spreadsheet D-019 to D-021 show fencing, 24/7 guards and trespass logs preventing access to contamination; NCP 40 C.F.R. 300.415(b)(2)(iv) lists fences/security as removal actions (recalled). Vulnerabilities we must scrub before conceding or defending: $310,000 "environmental litigation" fees (D-014/D-015/D-029 include "case defense," "Saxonbrook contribution claim preparation," settlement drafting); $125,000 internal staff time; $187,500 D-001 dated Oct. 2020 and soil-vapor work Nov. 2020, before the June 2021 AOC; D-016 "tender" Dec. 2023 vs notice of claim Feb. 22, 2024. Our March memo's cost breakdown (RI/FS $2.1M, interim $850k, prof. fees $200k) does not match the cost workbook (RI/FS $1.285M; interim $1.365M; env. legal $310k; coverage $680k; security $470k; EPA coordination $125k; misc. $65k); reconcile before any production. Counter: 38% x $3.62M = $1,375,600 (our floor ~$1.3M); at 30% Saxonbrook pays $1,086,000, below the floor. Hold 38%.
I. NRD (6.5; email 5). $400,000 credit: ROD Sec. 5 allows credit only for restoration pre-approved in writing by the trustees (DOI/FWS, NOAA, Oregon) and incorporated into the Restoration Plan; the 2022 project was voluntary and unapproved, and the federal trustees do not sign this decree. Orig. para. 57 barred credits. Also the credit is shared 70/30 (Cascade pays $1.96M, down only $24,000, while Saxonbrook falls $376,000). Reject unless trustees approve in writing; if approved, credit Saxonbrook alone.
J. Oversight cap (6.4.3). $1.2M total including $820,000 past leaves $380,000 for 10-15 years at est. $150-250k/year ($1.5-3.75M). Excess "only on further Court order" is unworkable for EPA. Counter: $2-3M future cap, exclusive of past, with adjustment mechanism (our flex).
K. Stipulated penalties (11.1-11.3; email). Halved rates ($750/$1,500/$2,500 vs $1,500/$3,000/$5,000) and a 15-day cure for all noncompliance. Accept a 10-15 day cure for performance only, never payments (our flex); rates: floor $1,000/$2,000/$3,500; reject 11.3.2 exclusivity (also bars CERCLA 122(l) penalties; contrary to orig. para. 91).
L. Work takeover (12). 90-day cure plus 30-day notice (vs 30 days); 100% vs 150%. Counter 120-125%, 30-day cure for Cascade/EPA; keep 12.1.2. Force majeure (15): restore financial-inability and increased-cost exclusions, payment obligations never excused (orig. 105, 107); notice 7-14 days; EPA decides.
M. Indemnity (13). 13.1 uncapped Cascade indemnity of Saxonbrook and Affiliates, including pre-2003 contamination; 13.2 Saxonbrook capped at $5M; this reverses our mutual uncapped scheme (orig. 81-85) and ignores that ROD attributed post-2014 mass to Saxonbrook. Reject; restore mutual, proportional, uncapped.
N. Arbitration (16). Reject (our firm term): judicial consent decree; Court retains jurisdiction and EPA is party. Keep mediation, then Court. Governing law (21): reject Oregon law; consent decrees are federal-law instruments (orig. 131-133).
O. Anti-assignment (3.2, Art. XX). Reject asymmetry; restore orig. 26-29 with EPA/DOJ approval for both; no release on assignment; delete duplication. Accept 10.2.4, 10.2.5, 10.1.1 and 22.3 only after EPA review.
P. Overruns (5.1.3, 5.2.2). 70/30 applies to all overruns; reject until 7.1 is resolved.

TIER 3 - ACCEPT / MINOR
Accept: comma and "premises" corrections, "Settling Parties" terminology, 104(a) citation, "Consent Decree" cleanup, date standardization, 24.2, 23.3, 23.5 ESIGN, 10.3.1, 2.17, 22.1 address after verification. Accept with edit: 1.1, 1.17 (delete "beyond obligations assumed"), 2.1 Affiliate definition (only if not used to extend protection), 4.1. Reject: 1.8 (false: Saxonbrook disposed 2014-2017 and contributed 38% of CVOC mass; ROD 2.1), 1.4 "arranged ... services agreement," 1.12 (accept arranger characterization only if "owner and operator" retained, ROD 6.1), 1.14-1.15, 2.19, 3.1, Cascade signatory change, 6.2 (31st-day interest holiday contradicts our para. 40), 10.4.1, 23.1.

4. NEGOTIATING PRIORITIES AND TRADES
(1) Reject all Tier 1 items in a single response letter and propose a call with Hale. (2) Offer: $680,000 concession; performance-only cure; oversight cap; penalty rates within floors; secured installments (max three). (3) Log all positions in the running issues list.

5. NEXT STEPS
1. Demand a certified machine comparison and corrected caption (Saxonbrook, not Vanguard); state in reply that no unflagged change is accepted.
2. Notify Granite Bluff and seek written consent; confirm policy renewal after Oct. 1, 2024; protect privilege in sharing.
3. Re-run Board exposure model correcting the double count; seek updated authority.
4. Confirm facts with EPA (Dr. Lindquist) and DEQ before telling Hale what the government will or will not lodge; our March memo planned a pre-circulation call (July 2024); confirm it occurred.
5. Reconcile past-cost workbook and strip non-recoverable items before any production.
6. Obtain Columbia River Commercial Bank rating and Saxonbrook/Ridgecrest financial and ownership data.
7. Verify authorities flagged "not verified" before any outgoing letter.
